title: A Kenya Safari From the Netherlands Begins With Two Nonstop Flights a Day From Schiphol
meta_title: Kenya Safari From the Netherlands: Schiphol to the Mara

excerpt: A Kenya safari from the Netherlands, planned in euros: the KLM and Kenya Airways nonstops from Schiphol, Dutch travel advice and eTA rules, school holidays and three real Divulge itineraries.
content:
A Kenya safari from the Netherlands starts with a nonstop flight from Schiphol to Nairobi of about 8 hours 25 minutes, on KLM by day or Kenya Airways overnight, then an online Kenya eTA and a private week in the parks. Budget roughly €2,750-3,550 per person all in, depending on the route.

Dutch travellers want straight numbers: which flight, what the Ministry of Foreign Affairs says, and the full cost in euros. This guide answers those questions from our office in Nairobi and maps them onto real Kenya safari packages, including two routes that suit Dutch interests in conservation and active days out.

Quick Facts

  • Nonstop flights: KLM and Kenya Airways, Amsterdam Schiphol to Nairobi, about 14 a week between them (checked November 2026)
  • Flight time: about 8 hours 25 minutes for 6,674 km
  • Entry: Kenya eTA from US$30, with mandatory Kenyan travel health insurance added since 5 October 2026
  • Dutch travel advice: yellow for the safari circuit; red and orange only for specific regions and city districts
  • Time difference: Kenya is 2 hours ahead of the Netherlands in winter and 1 hour in summer
  • Typical budget: about €2,750-3,550 per person with flights, eTA and tips

Which Flights Go From Amsterdam to Nairobi?

For a Kenya safari from the Netherlands, two airlines fly nonstop from Schiphol to Nairobi: KLM and Kenya Airways, about twice a day between them, in roughly 8 hours 25 minutes. KLM leaves late morning and lands around 22:00; Kenya Airways leaves in the evening and lands at about 06:10.

Those times come from route data we checked in November 2026 (Amsterdam to Nairobi route data) and shift by season. Either way, a Kenya safari from the Netherlands needs no change of plane.

Day flight or overnight flight?

On the KLM day flight, a Kenya safari from the Netherlands begins with a hotel night near the airport and game drives from the next morning. The overnight Kenya Airways flight lands at dawn, so after a slow breakfast we can drive you straight to Amboseli or the Rift Valley the same day.

If you sleep badly on planes, take the day flight; for an extra day in the bush on your Kenya safari from the Netherlands, take the overnight one.

What Does a Kenya Safari From the Netherlands Cost in Euros?

A private 7-day Kenya safari from the Netherlands costs roughly €3,350-3,550 per person all in, and a 4-day fly-in conservancy safari about €2,750, using our published starting prices, a return fare near €750, the eTA with insurance and guide tips.

KLM's own route page listed Amsterdam to Nairobi fares from €729 when we checked in November 2026 (KLM Amsterdam to Nairobi), so €750 is a fair planning figure outside peak weeks. Our trip prices are in US dollars, converted at the European Central Bank reference rate of 1 euro to US$1.0963 on 24 November 2026 (ECB euro reference rates).

For each Kenya safari from the Netherlands in the table, the middle column assumes a €750 fare, about €70 for the eTA with its Kenyan health insurance, and US$10 per person per day in guide tips. Your own travel insurance is extra, and these are planning numbers rather than a quote.

What pushes the price up or down?

For a Kenya safari from the Netherlands, the month matters most. Dutch summer holidays overlap the July to October migration in the Masai Mara, so August is the dearest time for both KLM fares and Mara camps. Our Kenya safari cost guide breaks the daily rate down by lodge tier and season, and the Masai Mara balloon flight adds US$500 per person (about €456) if you want it.

Which Kenya Routes Suit Dutch Travellers Best?

Most guests on a Kenya safari from the Netherlands choose a private 7-day road safari, which fits two weeks off with travel days at both ends. First-timers usually take the classic southern route through Amboseli and the Masai Mara; repeat visitors and keen photographers often prefer the quieter north around Samburu.

Our 7-day Amboseli, Naivasha, Nakuru and Masai Mara safari is the route we suggest most often for a first Kenya safari from the Netherlands, with a private Land Cruiser, full board, all park fees and a Lake Naivasha boat ride. For a second trip, the Ol Pejeta, Meru and Samburu safari trades the migration for rhinos and the Samburu Special Five: Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, Beisa oryx, Somali ostrich and gerenuk.

Not sure which side of Kenya to pick?

Our Samburu vs Masai Mara comparison sets the two regions side by side. Choose the Mara for big cats and the migration, and the north if you dislike crowds or have seen the Mara before.

Can a Safari Be Low-Impact and Active?

A safari can be both, and many travellers ask for exactly that. Private conservancies around the Masai Mara limit vehicle numbers and lease land from Maasai owners, and they allow guided walks and night drives that the national reserve does not.

Our 4-day conservancy walking safari flies you to Mara Naboisho Conservancy for bush walks with Maasai guides, game drives and night drives, and its conservancy fees go directly to the Maasai landowners. A Kenya safari from the Netherlands that adds these three nights to a road trip gives you a quieter Mara without giving up the big cats. See our Mara Naboisho Conservancy guide and sustainable tourism in the Masai Mara.

Cycling in Hell's Gate

Hell's Gate National Park near Lake Naivasha is one of the few Kenyan parks you can explore by bicycle, past zebras, gazelles and warthogs and into gorges with steaming vents. Adding it to a Kenya safari from the Netherlands is easy: our 9-day Hell's Gate to Masai Mara safari builds a full day there before four nights in the Mara.

What Does the Dutch Government Advise About Kenya?

The Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs gives most of Kenya the colour code yellow, which means be alert to safety risks, and keeps red and orange for specific areas. The advice was last changed on 20 October 2026 and was still valid on 25 November 2026 (Dutch travel advice for Kenya).

Red, meaning do not travel, covers the Mandera, Wajir and Garissa regions near Somalia (except Wajir airport), mainland Lamu and Kiwayu island. Orange, meaning essential travel only, covers Marsabit and Moyale, the Tana delta and the coast strip near Malindi, a few Mombasa wards including Likoni, and the Nairobi districts of Eastleigh and Pangani. None of these lies on a standard Kenya safari from the Netherlands through Amboseli, Naivasha, Samburu or the Masai Mara.

What the advice means for a beach extension

For a Kenya safari from the Netherlands with beach days, we suggest Diani or Watamu and fly guests in rather than routing them by road through Mombasa's orange-coded wards. Our guide to safety on a Kenya safari covers the rest, and we re-check the advice before you fly.

Do Dutch Citizens Need a Visa for Kenya?

Dutch citizens need a Kenya Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA), applied for online before travel, not on arrival. Your passport must be valid for at least six months after departure with one blank page, and since 5 October 2026 a Kenyan travel health insurance policy is bought within the eTA application.

The eTA starts at US$30 per traveller on the official Kenya eTA website (checked October 2026). The Kenyan policy does not replace your own travel insurance for cancellation and evacuation. Before you book a Kenya safari from the Netherlands, our Kenya eTA guide walks through the form.

Vaccinations and malaria

No yellow fever certificate is needed when you fly directly from Amsterdam, but one is required if you arrive from a country with yellow fever risk; see our yellow fever requirements page. Malaria risk is rated high in most of Kenya, including safari areas and the coast, and low in Nairobi city (NHS Fit for Travel, checked November 2026). For a Kenya safari from the Netherlands, book a travel clinic or GGD appointment six to eight weeks ahead, and read our Kenya safari vaccinations guide first.

When Should You Go, Given Dutch School Holidays?

The best time for a Kenya safari from the Netherlands is July to October for the Great Migration in the Masai Mara, or January to March for dry weather and lower rates. Families follow the school calendar, which splits summer across three regions.

The dates below are the official 2026-2027 school holidays (Government of the Netherlands, checked November 2026); individual schools may differ slightly.

Dutch holidayDatesConditions in Kenya
Christmas (all regions)19 December 2026 to 3 January 2027Green after the short rains; busy and dear
Spring holidaySouth 13-21 February; North and Central 20-28 February 2027Dry, warm and good value
May holiday (all regions)24 April to 2 May 2027Long rains; lowest rates, wetter roads
Summer holidayNorth 10 July-22 August; Central 17 July-29 August; South 24 July-5 September 2027Dry season and the migration; book 6-9 months ahead

For a Kenya safari from the Netherlands, the South region's late summer slot is a quiet advantage: early September often still has the herds in the Mara, with slightly fewer vehicles than mid-August. Month-by-month detail is in our best time to visit Kenya guide.

Insider Tips

  • Match the flight to your sleep: the day flight means an airport night first; the overnight flight gives you an extra safari day
  • Pack soft bags: fly-in legs such as the Naboisho trip usually allow 15 kg per person in a soft bag
  • Carry US dollars: small, recent notes for tips; euros are harder to use in the bush
  • Check your region's dates: North, Central and South summer holidays start a week apart, which can change peak or shoulder pricing
  • Re-read the travel advice: check the Dutch government page again in the week before you fly, as colour codes can change

Frequently Asked Questions

Is there a direct flight from the Netherlands to Kenya?

Yes. KLM and Kenya Airways both fly nonstop from Amsterdam Schiphol to Nairobi, about twice a day between them, in roughly 8 hours 25 minutes. KLM usually leaves late morning and lands around 22:00, while Kenya Airways flies overnight and lands at about 06:10. Schedules change by season, so confirm the times when you book.

How much does a Kenya safari from the Netherlands cost?

A Kenya safari from the Netherlands costs about €2,750 per person for a 4-day fly-in conservancy safari in low season and roughly €3,350-3,550 for a private 7-day road safari, including a return flight near €750, the eTA with Kenyan health insurance and guide tips. August and Christmas cost more, and your own travel insurance is extra.

Do Dutch citizens need a visa for Kenya?

Dutch citizens do not need a traditional visa but must hold a Kenya eTA, applied for online before travel. It costs from US$30, and since 5 October 2026 a Kenyan travel health insurance policy is bought in the same application. Your passport must be valid for six months after departure and have one blank page.

Is Kenya safe to visit according to the Dutch travel advice?

The Dutch travel advice gives most of Kenya, including Amboseli, Naivasha, Samburu and the Masai Mara, the colour yellow. Red and orange apply to the Somali and Ethiopian border regions, mainland Lamu, the coast strip near Malindi and some districts of Mombasa and Nairobi. Standard safari routes avoid all of these, and we re-check the advice before you travel.

What is the best time for a Kenya safari from Amsterdam?

July to October is the best time for the Great Migration in the Masai Mara and overlaps Dutch summer holidays, though it is the busiest period. February, including the spring school holiday, is a strong alternative with dry weather and lower rates. The long rains from late March to May bring the lowest prices but wetter roads.

Final Thoughts

A Kenya safari from the Netherlands is simple to arrange: a nonstop from Schiphol, an online eTA and a private week in the parks for roughly €2,750-3,550 per person. Pick your flight by how you sleep, check your region's school holidays, then let us fit the route around both.
